published_source: Table 4 column 3, Marketing Science 37(1) (papers/mksc/mksc.2017.1051.pdf, read Nov 2): bins short_0_1 0.36 (0.03); medium_2_24 0.21 (0.029); long_25plus 0.2 (0.041). published_coef = equal-weight mean of the 3 printed bins (Hull's post summary over event_structure.post_summary); no SE of the mean is printed. The printed values agree with authors_code (exact re-run) to printed precision.

authors_code.source: replication agent's authors_regs.do (work dir code/): areg y adoption_shortterm adoption_mediumterm adoption_longterm _Iperiod*, abs(user_id) vce(cluster user_id) on the rebuilt preclean.dta with the authors' sample filters (tables.do line 253); fixest reproduces b and SE (fixef.K = 'full') to < 1e-11 and N exactly

treat_bins: authors' bins in event time (tables.do define_adoption_dummies, cutoffs lines 679-680): short run = weeks 0-1, medium run = 2-24, long run = 25+ since adoption, 1 only for adopters; reference = all pre-adoption weeks of adopters plus all weeks of matched never-adopters; no leads. Recorded in event_structure (Nov 2); the pipeline now estimates these bins directly. event_pre_min/event_post_max are the superseded legacy coding (single-week dummies 0..24 averaged, 25+ endpoint) and are ignored when event_structure is present.
in_abstract_intro_status: unverified (no abstract in frame.csv, no article text)
main_text_status: verified Nov 2: Table 4 of the published article (main text)
replication_status: exact: the authors' areg re-run (Stata 16) on the rebuilt matched sample matches every printed coefficient, SE and N (published article, Nov 2); fixest with event_structure reproduces it to < 3e-12
expected_twfe_source: Nov 2 event_structure: equal-weight mean of the authors' bin coefficients (authors_code; fixest with es_assign reproduces them to < 3e-12) divided by the population SD of y in the estimation sample (y_sd_regsample)
notes: EVENT version of Table 4 column 3 (program table_breadth, tables.do line 370). Outcome: log(unique genres), defined when plays_tot>0. Main sample (tables.do get_data_mainsample, lines 58-66): period > 4, overlap_min <= period <= overlap_max (common observation window of the matched pair), matched == 1; 896 users = 448 adopters + 448 matched never-adopters (1:1 Mahalanobis matching on the logit propensity index, min_period and max_period; mahapick top-3 then mahaselectunique, seed 12345; 59 of 507 adopters left unmatched). Matched controls carry their partner's adoption week in adopt_period but their adoption dummies are always 0, so gvar g_adopt is NA (never treated) for them. Authors' regression: areg luniq_genre adoption_shortterm adoption_mediumterm adoption_longterm _Iperiod*, abs(user_id) vce(cluster user_id); no controls, no weights. Estimation sample: 46688 user-weeks, 896 users; 448 adopters, of which 4 have no pre-adoption row in the outcome sample (always treated) and 2 no post-adoption row; 60 adoption cohorts (weeks) with both untreated and treated rows; never-treated row share 0.498; treatment absorbing, no switch-offs. Nov 2: the pipeline estimates the authors' bins (event_structure); the earlier single-week re-binning deviation is removed. data_provenance original: raw Last.fm CSVs shipped in the package (external/spotify_panel.csv, external/spotify_users.csv), rebuilt through the authors' importing_spotify_panel.do, matching.do and preclean.do (work copies with absolute paths; graphs, fitstat and coefplot commented out). Prepared file: mksc1051_mainsample.rds = preclean.dta restricted to the main sample plus g_adopt, adoption bins, adoption_one and the Table 8 rob_ outcomes.

event_structure.source: code/tables.do define_adoption_dummies (lines 284-298; cutoffs $cutoff_shortterm = 1, $cutoff_mediumterm = 24, lines 679-680) and make_regression_table (line 253): areg y adoption_shortterm adoption_mediumterm adoption_longterm _Iperiod*, abs(user_id). Event time periods_since_adoption = period - adopt_period (preclean.do line 65); the dummies are 1 only for adopters with periods_since_adoption in 0-1, 2-24 and 25+; no leads, so every pre-adoption week of an adopter and every week of a matched never-adopter is the reference. Weekly periods 5-66 have no gaps in any outcome sample, every adopter's g_adopt (7-66) is a sample week, so rel = t - g equals periods_since_adoption exactly.
event_structure.verified: fixest y ~ i(ebin, ref = 0) | user_id + period (cluster user_id) with es_assign on the run_spec time index reproduces the authors' areg bin coefficients (Stata re-run on the rebuilt matched sample, authors_code) to max abs diff 4.7e-13 (SE 1.4e-13); rel equals the authors' periods_since_adoption on every adopter row and the bins equal the authors' dummies on every row (0 mismatches). N 46688 vs authors 46688. The rebuilt sample equals the published one: N, users and all printed coefficients and SEs agree to printed precision (Nov 2, article PDF). Same sample as the pipeline (no switch-offs, no pre-sample adopters). Script: ~/did_packages/_work/mksc.2017.1051/output/nov2_event_structure_check.csv (scratch verify_1051.R).
